title: An invariant line in a rational representation of a triangular algebraic group
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $J$ an affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose that for some $n\geq1$ there is a closed immersion $J\hookrightarrow B_n$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], where $B_n(A)$ is the group of invertible upper triangular $n$-by-$n$ matrices over each commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Let $V\neq0$ be a finite-dimensional rational $J$-module: a $k$-vector space with a coaction $c:V\to V\otimes_k k[J]$ satisfying $(c\otimes1)c=(1\otimes\Delta)c$ and $(1\otimes\varepsilon)c=1_V$, where $\Delta$ and $\varepsilon$ are the coordinate maps of multiplication and identity. There exist a one-dimensional subspace $L\subseteq V$ and a group-scheme character $\chi:J\to\mathbf G_m$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$, such that $c(v)=v\otimes\chi^*(t)$ for every $v\in L$; here $t$ is the coordinate of $k[t,t^{-1}]$. In particular $L$ is a rational submodule and its action is by $\chi$ after every commutative $k$-algebra extension. Neither algebraic closedness of $k$ nor smoothness or connectedness of $J$ is assumed.

source.place: Definition 16.1 and Proposition 16.2(c) implies (a), printed pp.324--325; applies over any field, not only characteristic zero.

proof.text: The diagonal entries give a homomorphism $\delta:J\to T=(\mathbf G_m)^n$: the $i$th diagonal entry of a product of upper triangular matrices is the product of the $i$th diagonal entries. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] to factor it as $J\xrightarrow{q}D\xrightarrow{j}T$, with $j$ a closed immersion and $k[J]$ faithfully flat over $k[D]$. Put $N=\ker\delta$. Since $j$ is injective on all algebra-valued points, $N=\ker q$. On all such points this is $J\cap U_n$, where $U_n$ is the unitriangular group. The equations setting the diagonal entries equal to $1$, together with the closed equations for $J\subset B_n$, exhibit $N$ as a finite-type closed subgroup of $U_n$. It is normal since it is a kernel. No assertion about a section of $q$ is needed.

source.place: Proposition 16.2(c) implies (d), printed p.325; Theorem 3.34, printed p.75.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary], the given coaction is a homomorphism $r:J\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$, and restriction gives an $N$-coaction $c_N:V\to V\otimes_k k[N]$. Set $d(v)=c_N(v)-v\otimes1$ and $W=\ker d$. Choose a basis of the nonzero finite-dimensional $V$ and apply [lem-sfb-unitriangular-subgroup-rational-fixed-vector] to $N\hookrightarrow U_n$ and $r|_N$. It gives a nonzero vector fixed over every algebra extension. Evaluating at the universal point of $N$ gives $c_N(v)=v\otimes1$, so $W\ne0$.

source.place: Proposition 16.2(d) implies (a), printed p.325; Theorem 14.5(b) implies (a), printed pp.281--282; Remark 4.1, printed p.84.

proof.text: For every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, the vectors in $V_R=V\otimes_kR$ fixed by $N$ after every further $R$-algebra extension are exactly $\ker(d\otimes1_R)$. Indeed the universal point over $R\otimes_k k[N]$ tests precisely this equation, and evaluation at any point gives the converse. This kernel is $W\otimes_kR$. To check this without a finiteness assumption on $k[N]$, choose a vector-space complement $E$ of $W$ in $V$. The map $d|_E$ is injective. The singleton-family case of [lem-sfb-vector-space-tensor-family-zero-detection], with right factor the $k$-vector space $R$, makes $(d|_E)\otimes1_R$ injective. Tensoring the explicit decomposition $V=W\oplus E$ decomposes every tensor into its two components; $d\otimes1_R$ kills the first and is injective on the second. Its kernel is therefore exactly the first component.

source.place: Lemma 5.15, printed p.102, using the universal invariant-vector test of Proposition 4.31; its kernel/base-extension justification is written out here.

proof.text: For $g\in J(R)$, $w\in W\otimes_kR$, any $R$-algebra $R'$ and $u\in N(R')$, normality gives $g^{-1}ug\in N(R')$, whence $u(gw)=g((g^{-1}ug)w)=gw$. Step 3 implies $gw\in W\otimes_kR$. Applying the same reasoning to $g^{-1}$ shows that this restriction is an automorphism. Restrictions are natural in $R$ and obey the group law because the original action does. The dictionary therefore gives a rational representation $r_W:J\to\operatorname{GL}(W)$, and its inclusion in $V$ intertwines the coactions. The restriction of $r_W$ to $N$ is the identity on all algebra-valued points, hence is the trivial group-scheme homomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 5.15 and its conjugation formula, printed p.102; Remark 4.1, printed p.84.

proof.text: The groups $J,D$ are affine and of finite type by hypothesis and Step 1. After choosing a basis of the nonzero $W$, [def-sc-general-linear-group] presents $\operatorname{GL}(W)$ by the finitely generated algebra $k[x_{ab},z]/(z\det(x_{ab})-1)$, so it too is affine of finite type. Now $q^*$ is faithfully flat by Step 1, and $\ker q=N$ acts trivially by Step 4. Apply [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-group-quotient-universal] to $r_W$ to obtain $s:D\to\operatorname{GL}(W)$ with $r_W=sq$. By the dictionary let $b:W\to W\otimes_k k[D]$ be its coaction. The coaction on $W$ as a $J$-module is $(1_W\otimes q^*)b$: evaluating this expression at $x\in J(R)$ gives $s_R(q_R(x))=r_{W,R}(x)$, and evaluation at the universal point gives equality of coactions.

source.place: Proposition 16.2(d) implies (a), printed p.325; Theorem 5.13, printed p.101.

proof.text: Since $j:D\hookrightarrow T$ is a closed immersion, $k[D]$ is a quotient of $k[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_n^{\pm1}]$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This Laurent algebra represents the functor of $n$ independent units, namely $T$, and is spanned by its Laurent monomials. Each monomial $t^a$ has $\Delta(t^a)=t^a\otimes t^a$ and $\varepsilon(t^a)=1$, by the multiplicative-group formulas and multiplicativity of the coordinate Hopf maps. The quotient map preserves these formulas. Thus its distinct monomial images form a spanning set of group-like elements of $k[D]$. By [lem-sfb-coalgebra-group-like-independent] they are linearly independent, hence a basis $(e_i)_{i\in I}$. Coincident images are counted only once. Every $e_i$ is a unit: the image of $t^{-a}$ is its inverse.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(c), printed p.234; Proposition 4.23, printed p.93; the basis used in Theorem 12.12(a) implies (b), printed p.235.

proof.text: Choose $0\ne w\in W$ and expand $b(w)=\sum_i w_i\otimes e_i$ with finitely many nonzero coefficients in the basis of Step 6. The counit identity gives $w=\sum_i w_i$, so some $w_i\ne0$. Coassociativity gives $\sum_i b(w_i)\otimes e_i=\sum_i w_i\otimes e_i\otimes e_i$. Applying the coefficient functional of $e_i$ in the last factor yields $b(w_i)=w_i\otimes e_i$. These are finite expansions, so no infinite tensor sum or coefficient extraction is involved.

source.place: Theorem 12.12(a) implies (b), printed p.235, its two displayed comodule identities.

proof.text: Fix such an $i$. The unit $e_i$ defines a $k$-algebra map $k[t,t^{-1}]\to k[D]$, $t\mapsto e_i$. The group-like and counit formulas of Step 6 show that it respects multiplication and identity; the antipode identity in [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf] gives $S(e_i)e_i=1$, so it respects inverse as well. Thus it gives a character $\psi:D\to\mathbf G_m$. Set $\chi=\psi q$ and $L=kw_i\subseteq V$. This line has dimension one since $w_i\ne0$. Steps 5 and 7 give $c(w_i)=w_i\otimes q^*(e_i)=w_i\otimes\chi^*(t)$, and linearity gives the same equality for every vector in $L$. The dictionary's evaluation formula then gives the scalar $\chi_R(g)$ on $L\otimes_kR$ for every $k$-algebra $R$ and $g\in J(R)$, proving the rational-submodule and extension clauses.

source.place: Proposition 16.2(d) implies (a), printed p.325; Theorem 12.12, printed p.235; Remark 4.1, printed p.84.

The statement matches 16.2 (c)=>(a) over an arbitrary field with no added hypotheses, and the steps follow Milne's own route, (c)=>(d)=>(a). Step 1: the image factorization applies since J and G_m^n are affine of finite type; ker delta = ker q because j is a monomorphism; N is closed in U_n and normal. Step 2: the unitriangular fixed-vector node applies to N, and the universal point gives W != 0. Step 3: base change of invariants uses the singleton case of tensor zero-detection on a complement E. Step 4: Milne 5.15's conjugation, scheme-theoretic. Step 5: the faithfully flat quotient universal property applies (J, D and GL(W) affine of finite type; N acts trivially as a morphism). Step 6: Laurent monomials map to group-like elements with counit 1, and their independence over any field gives a basis of k[D]. Steps 7-8: Milne 12.12's two comodule identities, then the character t -> e_i via the antipode identity. Every cited statement says what its step uses, there is no cycle, and no SGA is cited. There are no new nodes. The duplicate search (trigonaliz, eigenline, common eigenvector) found only Lie-algebra, alg-closed or embedding nodes, none stating the item. Edge cases checked: n=1, trivial J, mu_p in char p, alpha_p, finite or imperfect k. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection is the generic Mathlib flatness leaf Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap, reached through the Hopf-subalgebra faithful-flatness node (Milne 3.31). It is not part of the trace formula or Poincare duality or their proofs, so I accept it. No fixes were made and tool_uses is empty.

lean.statement: theorem triangular_representation_eigenline {k : Type u} [Field k] (J : Scheme.{u}) [J.Over (Spec (.of k))] [GrpObj (J.asOver (Spec (.of k)))] [IsAffine J] [LocallyOfFiniteType (J ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (J ↘ Spec (.of k))] (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (i : J.asOver (Spec (.of k)) ⟶ GeneralLinearGroup (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) k) [IsMonHom i] [IsClosedImmersion i.left] (htri : ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] (x : points (J.asOver (Spec (.of k))) R) (a b : Fin n), b < a → (GeneralLinearGroup.homMulEquiv (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) k R (x ≫ i)).val ⟨a⟩ ⟨b⟩ = 0) (V : Type u) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [FiniteDimensional k V] [Nontrivial V] (c : CoordinateComodule (k := k) J V) : ∃ (L : Submodule k V) (χ : J.asOver (Spec (.of k)) ⟶ StandardGroupSchemes.multiplicative k), IsMonHom χ ∧ Module.finrank k L = 1 ∧ (∀ v : L, c.val v = (v : V) ⊗ₜ[k] (@id Γ(J, ⊤) (χ.left.appTop ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of (LaurentPolynomial k))).inv (LaurentPolynomial.T 1))))) ∧ ∃ r : NaturalRepresentation (k := k) J V, genericCoaction (k := k) J V r = c.val ∧ ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] (x : Γ(J, ⊤) →ₐ[k] R) (z : R ⊗[k] L), r.action R (coordinatePoint (k := k) J R x) (L.subtype.baseChange R z) = x (χ.left.appTop ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of (LaurentPolynomial k))).inv (LaurentPolynomial.T 1))) • L.subtype.baseChange R z
